biography: Carlos Falletti, born under the scorching sun of Rio de Janeiro, carries the fire of Brazil in his heart and his driving. His journey began not on asphalt, but on the sandy beaches of Copacabana, racing makeshift go-karts built from scavenged parts with his older brother, Ricardo. It was Ricardo who first recognized Carlos's raw talent, pushing him to enter local karting competitions. Early races were a brutal learning curve, marked by crashes and mechanical failures, but Carlos's unwavering determination shone through. A defining moment came at the Brazilian National Karting Championship in 2010, where he clinched victory with a daring last-lap overtake, a move that caught the eye of WB Motorsport scouts. Now, at 31, Falletti is a seasoned competitor in the top echelons of motorsport, a formidable presence on the track, pushing the boundaries of his machinery and his rivals. While a World Championship still eludes him, his relentless pursuit of glory continues to captivate fans worldwide.
drivingStyle: Falletti's driving style is best described as 'controlled aggression.' He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and an uncanny ability to extract maximum performance from his tires, often pushing them to the absolute limit. While he is not afraid of wheel-to-wheel combat, he is a calculating driver, carefully selecting his battles and exploiting any weakness in his opponents. He relishes the pressure of a close race, often finding an extra gear when the stakes are highest.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry fueled by numerous on-track collisions and accusations of unsportsmanlike conduct. Schmidt has publicly criticized Falletti's aggressive driving, leading to heated exchanges both on and off the track.

famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about heart. If you don't pour your soul into every corner, you're just driving in circles."
careerHighlight: Winning the Monaco Grand Prix in 2020 after a nail-biting duel with Adrian Schmidt, securing his first major victory and cementing his place as a force to be reckoned with.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Brazilian Grand Prix in 2021, a devastating blow in front of his home crowd, costing him a crucial championship victory.
